column4: The sun and moon shone together, and the harbor was bright enough for fishermen to mend their nets at midnight.
Two trees at the bus stop dropped so many seeds that a grove grew around the bench.
One enormous tree scattered seeds across a grove, and within a week a forest had swallowed the road.
A cyclist leaned against a tree to rest while a squirrel inspected her front basket.
A person fell asleep on an open book and woke with a map printed across his body.
A person found a crate stamped APPROVED and asked what was inside when it began to sneeze.
A person asked the lord of the castle for permission to dwell in its abandoned bell tower.
At customs, a traveler had to use a silver whistle to call the officer down from his tower.
A traveler from long ago stepped out of a photograph to borrow my umbrella.
A person volunteered to serve tea to the samurai guarding the snowbound bridge.
A person used a needle to attach a silver star one inch below the brim of a hat.
A stranded hiker had to trust a stranger's word that the tiny boat would float.
During a blackout, each person said the message aloud to transmit it down the stairwell.
One person stepped out of the line to give an example of the dance step.
A person raised a helmet to protect a stunned owl from falling hail.
The lone person shoveling snow at the temple gate was a samurai taking the first watch.
A person offered to accompany me halfway up the mountain, then waved goodbye at the split boulder.
A person stirred the pond with a silver spoon and watched the water change into ink.
Every morning, a girl poured a cup of water into the sea to repay the tide for its shells.
A sheep dipped a hoof in the water and sent a ripple across the entire ocean.
A white pebble tumbled from the cave when water from the spring burst out.
In enchanted water, a turtle could swim forever without growing tired.
The camp cook turned on the water and asked the children to wash their muddy hands first.
A firefighter used water to extinguish the bonfire just as its flames began to resemble a dragon.
One wave hit the seal so hard that water drummed against its skin.
The lord of the castle asked his guest to pour water into his crown for a thirsty sparrow.
A cobbled lane led down to the water, where floating lanterns marked the entrance to the harbor.
The diver discovered the reason for the rainbow on the water when she spotted oil leaking from a barrel.
A wizard put a bowl of water on a raised stand and asked the moon to heal the cracks in it.
A child went fishing after a silver fish leaped out of the water and landed in her hat.
A tiger rose from the water to give a performance on the circus high wire.
At dawn, the fire beneath the cliff had burned down to ashes, and a fox warmed its paws in the dust.
A lamp with a tiny blue fire inside lit the whole city block.
Two candle fires leaned toward each other and rose as one tall flame.
The baker stacked the loaves so high in the oven that the fire began to burn the top loaf.
A shining mirror above the fire tilted to illuminate the map painted on the ceiling.
At the school fair, pupils from every grade mingled under a tree hung with paper goldfish.
A low branch of the tree supported an entire squirrel orchestra.
In the public square, a pine tree grew straight through the roof of a telephone booth.
In a village where everything stood one inch tall, a fallen tree blocked three streets.
With a talent for sawing, the carpenter turned one fallen tree into enough lumber for a bridge.
The carpenter turned over a board cut from a crooked tree and found a map carved on the reverse.
The woodcutter used an ax to chop a hollow tree in two, and ten bats flew out.
The lord of the castle carved an entire tree into the pillar that held up his balcony.
Every morning, a crow took one plum from the tree and dropped a pebble in its place.
When a single peach fell from the bare tree in winter, the villagers took it as an omen of spring.
A tree tall enough to reach the far bank fell across the ravine and became a bridge.
A yellow kite flew sideways into a tree and stayed there all winter.
Two friends cut a fallen tree into a shelf that stretched between their bedroom windows.
After a snowfall, a fox looked out from its burrow and saw that the old oak tree had turned white.
A craftsperson lowered a lantern into a hole and found an empty room painted blue.
Eight mice squeezed through a hole in the roof to watch the dancers below.
For her research, a biologist dug a hole and found nine beetles sharing a single leaf for a roof.
A giant needle thrust through a hole in the ceiling and stitched the carpet to the floor.
A lamb poked its head through a hole in the cold kiln to watch the potter stack bowls.
In autumn, the farmer lit a fire beside the grain field and roasted chestnuts at dusk.
The seed that dropped from a grain stalk was so heavy it dented the bucket.
The grain department stamped a picture of a dipper on every sack it inspected.
Workers chewing grain with their mouths full somehow hummed in perfect harmony.
A mouse needed only a second to steal a few grains from the farmer's bowl.
With one sharp knife, the farmer harvested enough grain in a day to make a profit.
As the river rose, many hands helped shift sacks of grain to the top floor.
With her heart pounding, the farmer tried to think of a way to coax a sleeping bear out of the rice field.
At the fair, a male ox showed its strength by pulling a plow straight across the rice field.
The town added a whole block of houses with front porches overlooking the old rice field.
At dusk, the farmer set a small fire beside the rice field, then carried a lantern to the neighboring dry field to check potato rows before frost.
A paddy ridge divided the rice field in half so each family could flood its own side.
After a flood, a row of shellfish marked the boundary between two rice fields.
At the beach market, a diver used one large shell to buy a net with a silver handle.
With a talent for carving faces into shells, the artist gained enough wealth to buy an island.
Every shell in the ship's freight changed into a china teacup as it crossed the equator.
A vendor flipped a shell over to sell it once she saw the tiny painted portrait on its reverse.
The judges held the carver in such esteem that they awarded her a prize made from a rare shell.
A craftsperson carved little ships out of shells as a tribute to the harbor's first captain.
Guests added shells to a mosaic to spell out congratulations to the newlyweds.
After the captain divided the shells among the crew, the poor cabin boy finally had enough to buy shoes.
The next chest of shells gave the village enough resources to repair its bridge.
A mouth appeared on the gate and asked a question before it would open.
When the sun shone through the gate, the monk knew his brief interval of silence had begun.
A girl pressed her ear against the gate to hear the orchestra rehearsing inside.
The magician's greatest talent was making a squeaky gate close without a sound.
In her leisure hours, the guard sat beneath the tree by the gate and whittled birds.
A flash of lightning showed a person slipping through the gate with a crate of apples.
A woman could finally relax under a solid roof after spending a week in a leaking tent.
A pig built a house with a roof low enough to scratch its back every time it walked inside.
A child painted a different character on every shingle of the roof so birds could practice reading.
The guard patrolled every inch of the roof after a hawk stole the king's hat.
As soon as the family arrived under the new roof, each child raced to claim a room.
Each guest at the inn tied a ribbon to the roof beam before sitting down to supper.
The miser's wealth filled the attic so completely that coins spilled through the roof tiles.
A jeweler hid her treasure by replacing a missing roof tile with a slab of jade.
A traveler dragged a fallen tree under the shelter of a cliff and slept on it like a bed.
During a sudden downpour, the royal court crowded under the narrow shelter that surrounded the courtyard.
A warehouse built under a cliff sheltered one car big enough to carry a whale.
A fortune-teller opened a store under a cliff shelter and sold umbrellas whenever she predicted rain.
A clerk attached a copper sign to a rain shelter and declared it the new government office.
At evening roll call, a mouth on each lantern called the name of the person carrying it.
A smith lost her metal key in a bucket and found it stuck to a bar of magnetic iron.
At the captain's command, a sailor rang a small metal bell to guide the rowboat through the fog.
A tiny bird opened its mouth to chirp, and the sound came out as loud as a train whistle.
Each word of the poem was painted on a separate tile along the temple steps.
At the temple, a child used both hands to hold a candle taller than he was.
With a wave of her hand, the wizard made a broom sweep a ballroom full of confetti.
A tiny star was born inside the sun and rolled out through a sunspot.
At the temple, a beam of sunlight touched the bell rope when it was time for tea.
The sun rose ten minutes early so it could watch the balloon race.
A woman grew fond of the child who brought her a paper tulip every Tuesday.
At midnight, a blade of grass changed into a flower that smelled like peppermint.
The stationer stitched a family's surname onto a sheet of paper with red thread.
A child stretched a thread across the spring and watched its straight line bend whenever a frog hopped over it.
